description: Two parent-group IR estates relevant to this cell were not located to a confirmed URL: Société Générale (60% owner of Komerční banka, which reports KB inside International Retail Banking) and UniCredit SpA (parent of UniCredit Bank CZ&SK). Both were referenced only indirectly through third-party coverage in this pass.

Česká spořitelna's entire document estate sits behind a client-side SPA at /cs/dokumenty-ke-stazeni with numeric category IDs in the URL fragment. Category IDs were captured for 2022–2026 results sets, results presentations (18) and Debt Investors & MREL (1124), but the full category registry and the backing data endpoint are unmapped.

Earnings-call audio, webcasts and transcripts were confirmed only at parent-group level (Erste publishes audio and video webcasts per quarter). Whether Komerční banka publishes its own conference-call recording or transcript, and where, was not established — the financial calendar page references investor events but the artefact itself was not located.

UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia is a single legal entity covering both markets and files under both Czech and Slovak law, but this run's language scope is cs and en only. Slovak-language disclosure surfaces on unicreditbank.sk were seen in passing (annual report PDFs under /content/dam/cee2020-pws-sk/) and not pursued. The same applies to ČSOB's Slovak arm following the 365.bank combination.

ESEF/XBRL machine-readable filings were confirmed only for Komerční banka, from 2020 onward. Whether ČS, ČSOB or UniCredit Bank CZ&SK publish ESEF packages — and if so where — is unknown, since ESEF obligation attaches to issuers with securities on a regulated market, which all four have via debt even where equity is unlisted.

Two obvious pointer estates were repeatedly implied by evidence but not scouted, as they sit outside this cell: the Prague Stock Exchange / PSE issuer disclosure pages and the Czech National Bank's central storage of regulated information, which is the statutory repository the kurzy.cz and patria.cz mirrors appear to draw from.

Air Bank a.s. is one of the most strategically interesting challengers in the cell — PPF-owned, a repeated first mover on retail UX and pricing — yet this pass located only its consolidated annual report PDFs and its press room. No Air Bank quarterly ČNB/ČBA disclosure annex and no capital-adequacy filing was found, and the regulator-designated disclosure page does not link them. Its half-year position is visible only through PPF's 'Air Bank Group' combined results releases, which are unaudited and use a group perimeter that differs from the bank's own.

Two of the ten actors named in this coverage cell are no longer live banks: Max banka merged into Banka CREDITAS and Hello bank wound down its Czech operations. That leaves eight live actors, of which one (mBank) has no Czech statutory disclosure at all. The cell rationale's premise — a long tail of licensed banks each carrying full statutory annual-report duties — holds for only six of the ten named entities.

Fetching the ČNB list of bank mandatory-disclosure links established that it covers roughly two dozen banks, materially more than the ten named in this cell plus the big four handled elsewhere. This pass did not enumerate and classify the remainder, so an unknown number of second-tier and specialist Czech-licensed banks (including building societies and specialist mortgage or corporate banks) currently have no scout assigned.

The cell rationale specifically justifies a separate scout on the grounds that these banks disclose branch, ATM and digital-channel decisions that systemic banks bury. This pass found the channels where such news appears (each bank's press room, and Air Bank / Partners Banka releases that quantified mobile-app usage and client milestones) but did not locate any structured, comparable branch-count or ATM-network dataset per bank. ČNB ARAD and the payment-system statistics were identified as the likely home for aggregate channel data, but the specific series were not confirmed in this pass.

Local-language coverage was achieved for every live actor: Czech-language queries were the ones that surfaced the ČNB disclosure-link list, the Fio quarterly XLSX annexes, the Trinity Bank archive, the Partners Banka document hub, the Max banka merger evidence, the Hello bank exit and the mBank Czech press portal — none of which reliably surfaced in English. The reverse gap is real though: English-language disclosure in this cell is thin and uneven. MONETA and Trinity Bank (2020 onward) publish English annual reports, Raiffeisenbank maintains an /en/ tree and an English investor presentation, and Partners Banka publishes English annual reports; Air Bank, Fio banka and Banka CREDITAS were not observed publishing English editions of their statutory reports in this pass.

Pointer and regulator-side sources were covered well (ČNB disclosure-link list, JERRS with its web services and open data, the Central Repository of Regulated Information, Sbírka listin, the national open-data catalogue). Independent third-party assessment sources were not: no credit-rating agency coverage of these banks was pulled beyond noting that MONETA maintains a ratings page, no auditor-identity mapping was compiled, and no ČNB supervisory enforcement or sanction record was searched. Job postings, procurement records and vendor case studies — which reveal payments and core-banking technology decisions indirectly — were not explored at all.

Sources found in this pass disagreed on the timing of the Max banka absorption into Banka CREDITAS — press coverage placed the completed legal merger at 1 October 2024 with a transitional dual bank-code period, while CREDITAS's own 2025 results narrative described completing the Max banka integration during 2025. The maxbanka.eu archive is consistent with the earlier date (documents stop at FY2023 and Q3 2024) but does not state a merger date. Banka CREDITAS's acquisition of the Maltese MeDirect group was also identified as a major perimeter change affecting comparability, but its effective date and accounting treatment were not established.

Bank acquiring arms other than Komerční banka (KB SmartPay) and ČSOB (platbakartou.csob.cz) were not individually mapped to a source. Česká spořitelna, Raiffeisenbank, UniCredit Bank, MONETA Money Bank, Fio banka and Air Bank all touch card acceptance or issuing-side processing in Czechia, and several appeared only incidentally (a UniCredit product-terms PDF, a Fio terminal page) rather than as tracked sources.

Issuer processing and card-platform outsourcing — arguably the cell's most strategically important signal — has no dedicated source. No Czech-language term for 'issuer processing' surfaced in any search; Czech practice appears to use the English phrase or to describe it periphrastically ('zpracování karetních transakcí pro vydavatele', 'zpracovatelské centrum').

The cell's Czech-language coverage is solid for acquiring/merchant-facing terms but thin for processing/technical vocabulary, and there is no Slovak-language coverage even though several of these entities (Global Payments, Worldline, Nexi) run Czech and Slovak operations from shared Prague or Bratislava infrastructure.

No source was found that reveals acquiring market share or portfolio switches indirectly through third-party observation — for example merchant-side gateway/terminal technology detection across Czech e-shops, scheme (Visa/Mastercard) licensee or principal-member lists for Czechia, or PCI DSS validated-provider listings scoped to Czech entities. The 'reveals-indirectly' category is therefore under-served relative to the direct and pointer categories.

Because the WebSearch quota was exhausted before this cell began, all discovery ran through single-page Seznam.cz HTML results, direct URL probing and the ARES API. No pagination beyond the first result page was possible and no second search engine was usable (DuckDuckGo served CAPTCHAs, Mojeek returned 403).

Sbírka listin entry points were resolved and their subjektId values confirmed for seven entities, but the individual filing documents inside each collection were not enumerated, so the recency and completeness of each company's filings is unknown. Czech entities not infrequently file late or incompletely.

No search-engine discovery was possible in this run (WebSearch budget exhausted before the first query). Coverage rests entirely on first-principles URL hypothesis and snowballing, which cannot find actors that no fetched page links to.

The seed list omitted GP webpay (Global payments Europe, s.r.o.), which self-describes as the most-used payment gateway in Czech e-shops — found only by snowballing. If the single largest actor was missing from the seeds, other significant actors are probably missing too. Actors identified but NOT yet source-profiled in this pass: Shoptet Pay (launched 2021-09-01 per Lupa.cz), Worldline CZ as a direct entity, Barion, Pays.cz, Fondy, and the meal-voucher/benefit e-money issuers (Pluxee/Sodexo, Edenred, Up Česká republika, Benefit Plus) which are licensed instituce elektronických peněz in scope for the 'e-money institutions' half of this cell but were not investigated at all.

Instant-payment (okamžité platby) adoption — an explicitly stated goal of this cell — was not evidenced in ANY source inspected. No gateway published instant-payment volume, share or adoption data. Similarly, payment-method mix (card vs bank transfer vs wallet vs BNPL) was absent from every corporate source, including the two most likely candidates (Comgate blog, Shoptet press).

Three sources need collection machinery this slice did not establish: Revolut's newsroom (HTTP 403, needs headless browser), Worldline IR (JS-rendered, near-empty response to plain fetch), and WS JERRS (requires a commercial certificate from eIdentity/I.CA/PostSignum plus an electronically signed request to jerrsws@cnb.cz).

Local-language coverage was achieved for the domestic layer — cs terms (platební brána, tisková zpráva, pro média, výroční zpráva, účetní závěrka, obchodní rejstřík, sbírka listin, platební instituce, instituce elektronických peněz, odložená platba, objem transakcí, zprávy a média, pro novináře) were used throughout and drove most successful discoveries. However, Slovak-language coverage was NOT attempted despite being materially relevant: Besteron is NBS-licensed and passporting into CZ, and GoPay reports CZ+SK merchant counts jointly. Nothing was collected in sk.

Only one CZ trade-press pointer (Lupa.cz's 'Platební brány' tag, 22 articles) was profiled, and it proved highly productive — it independently dated the GoPay/Worldline ownership completion and surfaced Shoptet Pay. No other Czech outlet was inspected.

Several assertions in this slice are hypotheses carried forward rather than confirmed facts: dataor.justice.cz contents and formats (named in portal text, never fetched); whether or.justice.cz Sbírka listin documents are free PDFs (not confirmed on the landing page); whether Adyen's shareholder letters contain an EMEA/Europe volume breakout (not confirmed on the IR landing page); the exact filenames of GoPay's ucetni-zaverky-*.pdf files (a placeholder pattern was reported, deliberately not guessed); Comgate's 'Zmínili se o nás' correct slug; whether Adyen has a Prague office among its 28 cities.

The mandatory bilingual search-engine sweep was not performed at all because the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before this cell started. Prepared but unexecuted Czech queries included: 'Twisto tisková zpráva odložená platba obchodníci výsledky'; 'Skip Pay ČSOB odložená platba tisková zpráva integrace'; 'nákup na splátky online platba později Česko tisková zpráva integrace'; 'poskytovatel spotřebitelských úvěrů Česká republika hospodářské výsledky výroční zpráva'; 'kup teď zaplať později Česko podíl na trhu'; 'PlatímPak Raiffeisenbank odložená platba e-shopy'. Prepared English queries included: 'Czech BNPL buy now pay later press release merchant integration results'; 'Home Credit Group annual report Czech Republic consumer finance'; 'Czech Republic deferred payment provider market share 2026'.

The long tail of Czech consumer-credit providers was identified by name but not individually profiled: Zaplo Finance s.r.o. (ČLFA member), PROFI CREDIT Czech a.s., Creditstar Czech s.r.o., CreditPortal a.s., AvaFin Czech s.r.o., Simfina a.s. (all SOLUS members), plus Provident Financial CZ and Fair Credit. ČLFA states it has 14 licensed consumer-credit providers as members, so at least a handful remain unnamed here.

Foreign BNPL entrants into the Czech market were not investigated. Klarna, PayPo and similar pan-European providers were neither confirmed nor ruled out as active in Czech checkouts. Notably, none of them appeared in the Shoptet payments addon catalogue, which is suggestive of limited Czech platform penetration but is not proof of absence.

The 'wallet providers' half of the cell brief is materially under-covered. Twisto and Skip Pay were treated primarily as BNPL, and no dedicated pass was made on Czech wallet or stored-value propositions — Revolut CZ, Fidoo, Qerko and any bank-issued wallet arms were not examined, and the boundary against the card-acceptance cell was not tested.

Regulatory enforcement and supervisory output was not collected. ČNB sanction decisions, supervisory benchmark reports, the Zpráva o výkonu dohledu and the Zpráva o finanční stabilitě were all reasoned about as relevant categories but none were fetched; likewise, no court or arbitration records, no ombudsman (finanční arbitr) decisions, and no Česká obchodní inspekce consumer-protection actions.

Czech specialist personal-finance and retail-trade media were not fetched on this pass — Peníze.cz, Měšec.cz, Finparáda, Lupa.cz, e15, Hospodářské noviny, MediaGuru and retail titles are all plausible carriers of BNPL pricing comparisons and merchant-adoption reporting. Only CzechCrunch was reached.

No specific ARAD dataset covering consumer credit or non-bank credit providers was identified, because the ARAD entry point returned an empty JS shell. The sector-level quantitative series that would let provider claims be benchmarked therefore remains unlocated.

Non-duopoly card schemes operating in the Czech market were not scouted: American Express (americanexpress.com/czech, americanexpress.cz), Diners Club, JCB and Discover all appear as live links from the SBK/CardMag industry pages, indicating a CZ presence, but none was fetched or classified in this pass.

Interchange-fee and scheme-fee disclosure pages for the Czech market — which the schemes are obliged to publish under the EU Interchange Fee Regulation — were not located. Two candidate paths were tried: visa.cz/about-visa/interchange.html and /o-spolecnosti-visa/interchange.html (both 404), and mastercard.cz/cs-cz/podnikatele/podpora/mezibankovni-poplatky.html (403).

Wallet and tokenisation operators sitting on top of the card rails in CZ — Apple Pay, Google Pay/Google Wallet, Garmin/Fitbit Pay, and the schemes' Click to Pay deployment (a Click to Pay page exists at visa.cz/business/consumers/click-to-pay.html) — were not scouted as sources. They are neither banks nor vendors, so like the schemes they risk falling between cells.

This slice is heavily weighted to direct operator sources (ČNB, Visa, Mastercard, Bank iD) plus a small number of indirect/pointer sources. Aggregator and archive classes are thin: no news-aggregation feed, no RSS inventory, and no web-archive strategy was established for the schemes' press pages despite the demonstrated risk that scheme sites are bot-defended and that mirrors carry broken links.

Czech-language coverage is strong for ČNB, Visa CZ, Bank iD, SBK and CardMag. It is absent for the SEPA/EU layer, and no Slovak- or German-language comparator was scouted even though zbk.sk (the Slovak bank card association, the direct analogue of SBK) is linked from the SBK homepage and would provide a near-identical dataset for cross-border benchmarking.

Three of the highest-value targets in this cell (mastercard.cz, the EPC document library and register of participants, and the ČNB ARAD database) are all unreachable by plain HTTP fetching — two via 403 bot defence, one via a JavaScript SPA. No headless-browser collection capability was exercised or confirmed available during this scout.

Because zero keyword searches could be run, discovery was confined to what could be reached by domain guessing and link-following from a small seed set. Entire plausible source types for this cell were therefore never tested: Czech payments trade newsletters, LinkedIn/X accounts of the schemes' CZ country managers (SBK's own X account @SdruzeniK was seen but not assessed), scheme-sponsored CZ consumer research reports, and tender/procurement notices for national payment infrastructure.

There is no public source that splits the Czech ATM estate by owner/operator. ČNB reports only ATMs operated by Czech banks (4.9 thousand at end-2025); Euronet self-reports ~10% of a ~5,000 machine national total; SBK's whole-estate series stopped around 2011. The three cannot be reconciled without an operator-attributed dataset.

The core financial disclosures for every Czech actor in this cell (Euronet Services 25608452, Loomis Czech Republic 26110709, Brink's Cash Solutions (CZ) 27590151, Brink's Cash Solutions Services (CZ) 08829969) exist only as PDFs inside the court Sbírka listin — often scanned — and were not retrieved in this run. Chytrý rejstřík indicates 56 documents on file for Euronet Services alone.

Only the large, internationally-owned CIT operators were identified (Loomis, Brink's, plus the unresolved G4S question, and ČP Security surfaced incidentally as a money-transport provider). Smaller and regional Czech cash-transport and cash-processing firms were not enumerated, and no association directory covers them.

Discovery in this slice ran on a single engine (Seznam.cz), first page only, because the WebSearch budget was exhausted and DuckDuckGo/Mojeek were blocked. English-language and international-trade-press coverage of the Czech ATM/CIT market is therefore thin in this slice, and no result set was paged beyond the first ten hits.

Four high-value endpoints were not successfully retrieved — Euronet Worldwide IR, Brink's IR, SEC EDGAR (403), and the smlouvy.gov.cz search UI (timeout) — so parent-level segment disclosure and contract-level evidence remain unread for this cell.

Bank-to-deployer ATM outsourcing and network-participation agreements — the variable that determines how much of the nominally bank-operated Czech fleet is actually run by a third party — are undisclosed by both banks and Euronet. Similarly, bank–CIT cash-logistics contracts are private and outside the public contracts register.

No long-run Czech time series for the deployer-operated ATM estate or for CIT market size was assembled. ČNB's series covers bank-operated machines from 2021 onward in the commentary text, SBK's whole-estate series ends around 2011, and CardMag's archive is unindexed PDF.

Mandatory Czech-language (and English) search was not performed at all because the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before the cell started. Every seed query and every planned extension query went unrun; discovery relied entirely on fetching known domains, following redirects and enumerating sitemaps.

Two of the ten named seed actors remain uncharacterised or structurally silent: GEM System (redirect loop on all four URL variants attempted) and Unicorn (JS-rendered; sitemap shows no reference or investor section). Asseco Central Europe, the most important actor in the cell, is 403-blocked.

The cell's ten seed vendors are almost certainly not the full Czech bank-technology supplier population. No systematic expansion was performed, and one seed actor (CCA Group) turned out to have no banking references at all — evidence the list was assembled by reputation rather than from a register.

No demand-side public-buyer channel for state-controlled Czech financial institutions was successfully captured. The CNB procurement page 404'd on the path attempted, and no profil zadavatele was located for Ceska exportni banka (CEB) or Narodni rozvojova banka (NRB, formerly CMZRB) — even though the ICZ CEBIS reference proves CEB buys bespoke banking systems.

Non-web vendor disclosure channels were not examined at all: vendor LinkedIn company pages (where Czech integrators often announce bank wins before or instead of a press release), conference programmes and recorded talks (e.g. banking-IT conferences where bank CIOs present their vendor stack), vendor YouTube channels, and job postings that name the specific core-banking or payment platform a vendor is staffing for a named bank.

Vendor financial disclosure was identified as a channel (Sbirka listin, KKCG investor pages) but no actual filing was retrieved, and no vendor was resolved to an ICO in this slice. PDF availability and any open-data/API route for or.justice.cz were not confirmed on the search page.

Local-language coverage is uneven across the cell in a way that defeats a single monitoring rule. Monet+, ICZ and CCA publish primarily in Czech; Aricoma, Adastra and Unicorn maintain true CS/EN mirrors (/cs/tiskove-zpravy, /cs/success-stories/, /cs/); Trask and Profinit publish in English only despite being Czech companies; Asseco's language structure is unknown because the site is blocked.

Zero search-engine queries were executed for this cell (WebSearch budget pre-exhausted; DuckDuckGo CAPTCHA, Mojeek 403, Bing RSS cache-collided). Every candidate here was reached by domain reasoning, direct navigation or on-site search, so the long tail of vendors and the entire class of 'sources I did not already know to guess' is unexplored.

Named-but-unreached in this pass: Fiserv (timeout), Finastra (403), Printec (403), Thales Group corporate (empty body), Euronet (path migrated). Reasoned-about but never fetched at all: ACI Worldwide (aciworldwide.com/news-and-events 301s to investor.aciworldwide.com/events-and-presentations; the news-releases path then timed out), Worldline (two path guesses 404'd), NCR Voyix, Nexi, Backbase, Mambu, Thought Machine, Sopra Banking Software, Tietoevry, Hyosung TCS, GRGBanking, KAL ATM Software, Cennox, IDEMIA, Giesecke+Devrient, BS/2 (Penki kontinentai), Asseco SEE.

The earnings-call TRANSCRIPT channel — explicitly named in this cell's rationale as where vendors mention country deployments — has no source assigned. IR pages give decks and webcast links, but searchable transcript text (where a CFO says 'Czech Republic' in Q&A) sits with third parties: Motley Fool, Seeking Alpha, Quartr, AlphaSense, Koyfin, and the vendors' own webcast providers. None was evaluated.

Vendor LinkedIn newsrooms and regional/country LinkedIn pages are unassessed. For this cell they matter disproportionately: CEE country organisations and local sales teams frequently post a Czech customer win on LinkedIn that never reaches the global newsroom, and LinkedIn is the practical fallback for the vendors whose own sites are WAF-blocked (Finastra, Printec). Vendor LinkedIn URLs were observed on Diebold Nixdorf, Temenos, Comarch, Bankovnictví and Protext pages but none was evaluated.

Czech-language coverage rests on exactly three verified portals (Protext, Bankovnictví online, SystemOnLine) and no cs-language keyword search was ever executed against any index. Nine constructed Czech terms remain unexercised: platební terminál, jádrový bankovní systém, samoobslužná zóna, recyklace hotovosti, výroční zpráva, případová studie, nasazení, implementace, dodavatel.

Only three machine-friendly feeds were confirmed across the entire cell: NCR Atleos IR RSS, Auriga /en/feed/, and ATM Marketplace /rss/. Global Payments IR advertises an RSS feed. Everything else is JS-rendered (Diebold Nixdorf IR), WAF-gated, or offers no feed at all (FIS media room showed none).

The NCR Atleos investor archive (RSS plus numeric /detail/<id>/ URLs) is exposed to the pending Brink's acquisition, and the Euronet news path has already migrated in a way that broke its own redirect (301 to a 404). No snapshotting has been done for either.

Zero search-engine queries were executable in this cell because the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before the first call. Discovery relied entirely on domain guessing plus link-graph snowballing.
English-language mirrors were identified but not systematically enumerated or compared against their Czech originals.
Member-only tiers were identified at three associations but their contents remain uncharacterised.
Historical member rosters were not captured; only current-state snapshots were observed.
Insurance and crypto-asset representation in the Czech financial-sector association map is unresolved.
Association working groups, committees and named officeholders were located but not harvested, leaving the people layer of the actor map empty.
No URL in this slice has been confirmed reachable by an independent verification pass, and several were reached only via redirects or non-obvious entry points.

The mandatory Czech-language search sweep of the cell's seed queries was never executed because the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted at the first call. Discovery ran entirely on direct fetch plus link-snowballing.

Smaller and non-bank financial actors were not swept: credit unions (spořitelní a úvěrní družstva), small licensed payment institutions and e-money issuers, PSD2 third-party providers, and fintechs such as buy-now-pay-later and payment-gateway startups. Only Comgate was confirmed among pure-play PSPs.

English-language and international distribution of Czech financial announcements is unmapped. It is unknown whether Czech banks or PSPs use GlobeNewswire, Business Wire, PR Newswire or EQS for English releases, although Protext itself claims reach into media in nearly 180 countries and offers an English-language filter.
The downstream mirror graph is unmapped. Protext states distribution to 27 Czech news portals, and ceskenoviny.cz/pr/ was confirmed as one of them, but the other mirrors were not enumerated.

Four high-value targets are behind bot defences or transport failures and have no confirmed collection route: ČSOB (HTTP 500 on all paths), UniCredit Bank CZ (403), Banka CREDITAS (403), Mastercard CZ newsroom (403), plus Anopress and Monitora (TLS errors).

Licensing terms for bulk collection are unresolved for every archive in this cell: ČTK/Protext content reuse, ČTK Infobanka, NEWTON Media archive (1989-present), Anopress and Monitora. Robots and terms-of-use were not inspected for protext.cz or ceskenoviny.cz.
The PR-agency layer was identified (APRA member directory, Mediář agency index) but not harvested, so the mapping from agency to financial-sector client has not been built.

Archive depth is confirmed only for a few sources (Protext finance category around 440 pages and roughly 50,525 total records; ČNB 1997-2026; MONETA back to about 2015; NEWTON archive advertised from 1989). Depth is unknown for KB, Česká spořitelna, Raiffeisenbank, Air Bank, Fio and mBank CZ because their listings did not render.
No search-engine discovery was possible (WebSearch budget exhausted at 200/200 before this agent ran), so the six seed queries and their planned cs/en extensions were never executed.

Two outlets explicitly named in the cell brief — iDNES Ekonomika and Lidovky — could not be reached at all because the fetch tool blocks the MAFRA hosts. Their RSS paths, section structure and paywall model are unknown.

Broadcast and audio were only partially covered. ČT24's economy desk was verified, but Czech Radio's business output (Český rozhlas Plus / Radiožurnál business slots, ČRo's 'Zaostřeno'-style formats) and the fast-growing Czech business-podcast layer (HN podcasts, Seznam Zprávy podcasts, Info.cz's large podcast slate, CzechCrunch audio) were not mapped. Bank CEOs give figures and forward guidance in podcast interviews that appear nowhere in text.

Newsletter products were not mapped. Czech business newsrooms increasingly put their best analysis in paid newsletters (HN's business newsletters, Ekonom's Wednesday newsletter observed on-site, Deník N's 'Ranních 5 minut', E15 and CzechCrunch mailings) which are not on the public web and are not indexed.

No actor map of individual Czech banking/finance journalists was built (bylines, their outlet moves, and their personal X/LinkedIn/Bluesky accounts where scoops often break minutes before the article). MediaGuru was identified as the pointer that would support this but its /lide personnel feed was not mined.

English-language CZ business coverage is thin in this slice: only Expats.cz was verified, Radio Prague International returned 403, and other English titles (Prague Morning, Brno Daily, the English output of Czech agencies) were not reachable without search.

Specialist finance/investment media that a naive scout would sweep up here — Patria.cz, Kurzy.cz, Investiční web, Roklen24, Měšec.cz, Peníze.cz, Bankovnípoplatky.com — were deliberately NOT claimed by this cell, which is scoped to general business/economic media. They were also not verified, so nothing should be assumed about them from this slice.

The compliant full-text route for paywalled and print-only CZ coverage is unresolved. Newton Media was verified as offering a licensed CEE archive, but Monitora and Anopress could not be reached, and no pricing, API capability or redistribution terms were established for any of the three.

Virtually all Czech-segment data in this cell is locked inside PDFs (quarterly reports, presentation decks, URDs, country sheets). Only Erste (XLSX data sheets), KBC (results table / ESEF XBRL), RBI (XLSM) and SG (quarterly series) offer structured alternatives.

Local-language coverage of this cell is structurally thin, as documented in the negative findings. cs-language terms were successfully used and did surface the relay layer and Czech-law prospectuses, but no parent publishes IR content in Czech.

The CRD Article 89 country-by-country reporting annexes — which give Czech Republic turnover, profit before tax, tax paid and FTE headcount on a uniform basis across Erste, KBC, SG, UniCredit, RBI and BNP Paribas — were reasoned about and are known to sit in group annual reports/URDs, but the specific annex pages were not individually located and page-anchored in this pass.

Historical depth was only established for Erste (reports reportedly back to 1997) and Euronet (EDGAR filings back to at least 2004). Archive depth for KBC, SG, UniCredit, RBI, PPF and Worldline was not determined.

Only the Austrian OAM (OeKB) was identified and verified. The equivalent statutory archives for the Belgian (KBC), French (SG, BNP Paribas, Worldline), Italian (UniCredit) and Dutch (PPF's former N.V. entities) parents were not located in this pass.

Two perimeter/identity changes in this cell threaten archive continuity: PPF Group N.V. became PPF GROUP a.s., and PPF Financial Holdings B.V. became PPF Financial Holdings a.s. Erste's acquisition of Santander Bank Polska (now Erste Bank Polska) also changes the segment mix against which the Czech segment is compared.

Two access frictions were observed or inferred: unicreditgroup.eu HTML pages appear WAF-protected (403), and the most analytically useful third-party layers (Patria research, Seeking Alpha, Quartr) are paywalled.

No keyword search of any kind was possible (WebSearch budget exhausted at the first call), so the six assigned seed queries were never run and no result-page snowballing occurred. Discovery relied entirely on URL hypothesis, first-principles category inference and on-page navigation snowballing.

The English-language leg of the mandate is entirely unfulfilled. No en-language query was run, so English-language coverage of the Czech banking market - the trade press that writes about CEE banking in English, and English-language editions or summaries produced by Czech outlets - was not assessed at all.

No Czech banking or personal-finance PODCAST, YouTube channel or newsletter-first publication was identified. Executive interviews about technology and payment strategy - exactly what the cell rationale calls out - increasingly appear in audio/video formats and in email-first products rather than on indexable article pages. Poradci-sobe.cz and profipf.cz were observed to carry podcast/video strands, and bankovnictvionline.cz has an app, but no standalone audio/video source was mapped.

Branch-closure and ATM-network-change coverage is the weakest verified strand in this cell relative to how central the cell rationale makes it. bankovnipoplatky.cz's section listing mentions branch closures, and Mesec.cz's tables carry per-bank ATM withdrawal charges, but no source was found that systematically tracks Czech ATM COUNTS or branch counts over time. The Kurzy.cz /bankomaty/ vertical, which might do exactly this, did not render.

The two highest-value institution-facing trade titles in this cell are subscription-gated: Bankovnictvi (bankovnictvionline.cz) shows preview excerpts with full text behind 'CELY CLANEK'/Predplatne, and PROFI Poradenstvi & Finance gates its magazine. FOND SHOP is likewise paywalled. The executive interviews that motivate this cell are therefore only partially readable.

RSS/feed availability was confirmed for exactly one source in this cell (Mesec.cz at https://www.mesec.cz/rss/clanky/, valid RSS 2.0, excerpt-only items). Every other candidate's feed status is unknown - most homepages advertise only email newsletters, and no /rss/ probing was done beyond Mesec.cz.

No Czech-language source dedicated to the MERCHANT/acquiring side of payments - payment terminals, card acceptance pricing, POS technology - was found as a specialist outlet. Podnikatel.cz is the closest proxy and covers it only incidentally; SystemOnLine covers bank-side IT rather than merchant acceptance. Given this run's payments scope, the acceptance layer is materially under-covered.

Publisher/operator identity is unresolved for two candidates that would otherwise rate higher: bankovnipoplatky.cz (no imprint surfaced on the pages fetched, despite it being the most on-topic fee watchdog in the cell) and fintechcowboys.cz (ownership not disclosed). Credibility scores for both are capped by this rather than by anything observed about their content.

No search-engine-mediated discovery was possible in this run (WebSearch budget exhausted before the first call). Every source here was reached by guessing a domain or by snowballing from an already-known page, which structurally favours large incumbent outlets.

The 'fintech-focused podcasts' half of this cell is essentially unfilled. Only general-business and general-tech shows were confirmed (CzechCrunch Money Maker, Lupa.cz podcast, HN's MoneyPenny and Krypto Insider). No dedicated Czech fintech or payments podcast was verified, and the hypothesised association-linked 'FinTech Roadmap' show was not found on the association's site.

Six named targets could not be read: Forbes.cz (JS-rendered, empty bodies on three paths) plus five HTTP 403s (Peníze.cz, Investiční web, Živě.cz, Ecommerce Bridge CZ, Finmag.cz). Forbes CZ is named directly in the cell brief and Ecommerce Bridge is the only merchant-acceptance-side title identified.

Four confirmed sources in this cell run subscription tiers whose gated content was never assessed: Hospodářské noviny+ (predplatne.hn.cz), e15 Premium (/e15-premium), Lupa+ (/podporte/), and the print/digital edition of Časopis Bankovnictví (/predplatne). The gated layer is likely where the substantive banking and vendor detail sits.

Every confirmed outlet is Prague-centred national media. No regional Czech startup or tech media were identified — Brno (a substantial tech hub, and the venue for the CryptoNight event the association listed), Ostrava and Plzeň all have startup ecosystems whose local coverage was not probed at all.

English-language coverage of Czech payments rests on two pan-regional outlets (Tech.eu, The Recursive) whose Czech output is intermittent and skewed toward VC deal news. No Czech-domiciled English-language business publication was identified, and CzechCrunch showed no English edition in the structure retrieved.

No Czech VC-published or data-provider-published funding report was located. The depo.ventures hypothesis failed at DNS, and no equivalent Czech startup funding report publisher was confirmed. CzechStartups.gov.cz has a /startup-data/ path that was seen referenced but not itself retrieved and parsed.

The Czech terminology used was derived from site navigation rather than tested for precision and recall. High-precision regulatory and acceptance-side terms — 'platební instituce', 'poskytovatel platebních služeb', 'licence ČNB', 'akvirer', 'POS terminál', 'okamžité platby', 'otevřené bankovnictví', 'PSD2' — were never run against any index, while the high-recall term 'platby' demonstrably returns noise.
No search-engine querying occurred in this slice (WebSearch budget exhausted before the first call), so the cell was covered by seed-actor fetching and snowballing only.
Moody's, S&P and Fitch are all blocked to unauthenticated automated fetch, leaving the rating-action layer of this cell undelivered despite being its highest-credibility component.
ESMA's European Rating Platform and CEREP could not be located; three hostname/path guesses failed and the confirmed ESMA CRA hub does not link them.

Only three Czech-market listed banks (Komerční banka, Moneta Money Bank, Erste/Česká spořitelna) have identifiable analyst-coverage pages. Large unlisted Czech banks — ČSOB (KBC), Raiffeisenbank CZ, UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia, Air Bank/Home Credit, Fio banka, Trinity Bank — have no equity analyst layer and are visible to this cell only through rating actions and press mirrors.

No Czech-language rating-agency commentary or local rating agency was identified. Historic Czech agencies (e.g. CRA Rating Agency, later absorbed into Moody's) and any smaller ESMA-registered agencies rating Czech institutions were not investigated.

The run scope is sector=both, but every candidate found is banking-equity or bank-rating oriented. No sell-side or rating coverage of Czech payments actors (card schemes, PSPs, acquirers such as ČSOB/Global Payments JV, Comgate, GoPay) was identified.

Legal status is 'unclear' or 'restricted' for nearly every candidate. Patria, Kurzy.cz and Akcie.cz terms of service were not read, and rating-agency press releases carry explicit redistribution restrictions.

Zero Czech-language discovery was performed for this cell because the session-wide web-search budget was exhausted before the agent's first query. The cell's own Czech seed query was never run, and no Czech glossary/actor-map terms were exercised against a search engine.

Six candidates (Reuters, Bloomberg, The Banker, Radio Prague International, CEE Legal Matters, FinTech Futures, plus MarketScreener and the intellinews Czech country page) could not be inspected due to 403s or tool-level domain blocks. Their section URLs, feed availability and paywall mechanics are unknown.

Paid English deal-intelligence and filings-aggregation services that would systematically capture Czech banking M&A and licence events - Mergermarket/ION Analytics, LSEG/Refinitiv Deals, S&P Capital IQ, Dealogic, PitchBook - were not assessed at all this run.

No per-issuer mapping was built. Which specific Czech banking and payments entities each international outlet actually names - and therefore which entities are reliably visible in English at all - remains unknown, since entity-level searching was impossible.
Feed availability is confirmed for only one outlet in this cell, and no robots.txt or rate-limit posture was checked for any domain.

The statutory basis for the cell ended on 30.6.2025 and the successor (EBA Pillar 3 Data Hub) covers a different, CRR-scoped population — 'large and other institutions' — which will not include every small Czech bank, building society or credit union currently in the cell.

Five institution pages (ČSOB, ČSOB Hypoteční banka, UniCredit, Banka CREDITAS, ČSOB Stavební spořitelna) refused automated fetches with 403/500, and two more (Česká spořitelna, Air Bank) require JavaScript rendering. That is seven of the largest names in the sector, including two of the four systemically important banks.
Three ČNB link-indexes (investment companies, pension companies, and 25 of the 35 securities dealers) and the EBA P3DH public portal remain unenumerated.

The building-society tier (stavební spořitelny) was covered opportunistically via the ČNB index rather than through its own local-language search sweep, and two of its five members (ČSOB Stavební spořitelna, Modrá pyramida) could not be reached at all. Group consolidation is actively moving these entities onto parent-bank domains (Buřinka→burinka.csas.cz, Modrá pyramida→KB infrastructure, ČMSS→csobstavebni.cz), so their disclosure locations are unusually volatile.

The cell is overwhelmingly Czech-only by legal design — the decree required publication in Czech — and no English mirror of the quarterly template was found at any Czech-owned institution. The only English-language disclosures observed were at the third-country branches (Bank of Communications Prague, in English and Chinese) and in some parallel annual reports (Trinity Bank, RSTS).

No web-archive fallback was identified for this cell. Given that entities are demonstrably disappearing (Max banka, and disclosure pages being folded into parent-bank domains), and that the legal duty to keep publishing has lapsed, historical quarters are at real risk of vanishing without a snapshot.

The comparability claim underpinning the cell — that the template is machine-comparable across all institutions — has not been tested against actual files, across issuers or across the 2014/2017/2021 amendments.
The Burzovní věstník (ftp.pse.cz/Vestnik.doc) and the issuer master-data branch (ftp.pse.cz/Issuers.dta) are 401-gated, removing the exchange's authoritative gazette from automated reach.
The JSON/XHR endpoint that backs the BCPP news search and the Event Calendar was not identified, so the two most time-sensitive surfaces in this cell currently have no cheap collection route.

Several ftp.pse.cz branches with recent modification dates were not opened in this run: Cdcp.dta, IssuersCDCP.dta, Member.dta, Results.act, Results.ak, Results.old, Service.dta, Tom.dta, Info.bas/CEEplus (mtime Aug 2026), Info.bas/Indexy (Jul 2026), Info.bas/RTS_27, Info.bas/XETRA_T7, Info.bas/Eng, Info.bas/Statistiky, and Info.bas/News subfolders including a 2025-09-01 directory.

Files in Annual.rep and Semiannual.rep are named by abbreviated BCPP issuer codes (ICBA, RZBCL, CSPOL, TRIREL, CEZ, KOFOL, TELECL, …) rather than ISINs, and no public code→issuer→ISIN mapping table was located. Without it, the two largest filing archives cannot be reliably filtered to financial-sector issuers.

The ČNB OAM/CÚRI repository was identified and its legal basis and content categories confirmed, but its search form, per-issuer result URL structure, pagination, and any bulk/export capability were not exercised in this run — only the entry-point URLs were captured.

START-market disclosure material is predominantly Czech-only: the Start Day presentations, the PX Veřejná nabídka user guide and description (both May 2025) and the sponsored analytical reports have no confirmed English counterparts, while only the older START public-offering rules (v2.0, Nov 2020) exist in English. Coverage of the SME/fintech tripwire therefore depends entirely on Czech-language collection.

The debt-securities segment lists name the bank issuers (Moneta, Raiffeisenbank, UniCredit Bank, J&T Banka, J&T Finance Group) but were not traced through to each issuer's prospectus, base prospectus, or issuer-level disclosure pages. These are exactly the banks that carry disclosure duty without listed equity, so the linkage is the highest-value unfinished work in this cell.

The cell's core premise — that the exchange timestamp is worth having because IR pages get edited or withdrawn — has no baseline: no snapshot of BCPP announcement text versus issuer IR text has been taken, so divergence cannot yet be detected.
The ČNB Central Storage (OAM) offers no documented API, RSS feed or bulk export; it is a form-driven Oracle web application. Every regulated filing must be reached through session-bound queries.

This cell established WHERE the CZ payment institution / EMI / small-scale PSP registers live (JERRS, PSRI list, EBA PSD2 register) but did not extract the actual entity roster or counts, and did not confirm which JERRS role codes correspond to each of the four Czech payments licence categories.

JERRS presents current status (valid / suspended / revoked) and offers aggregate counts and creation/termination time series, but it is unclear whether per-entity historical states (previous names, past authorisation scopes, withdrawal dates) are retrievable retrospectively.
English interfaces exist for OAM (/cnb/oam_en), JERRS (/cnb/jerrs_en) and the ČNB lists hub, but whether the English content and lists are updated in step with the Czech originals was not tested.

Branches of foreign banks and passported EEA payment institutions operating in CZ typically disclose in their home member state's OAM rather than in the ČNB storage, and this cell did not map which CZ-active entities fall into that category or where their filings actually land.

Registers of pověření zástupci (payment service agents), vázaní zástupci and samostatní zprostředkovatelé — fed through REGIS and surfaced in JERRS and the open data — were identified but not enumerated. These reveal distribution networks and white-label payment arrangements that are otherwise invisible.

The date coverage of the ČNB prospectus register and of the final-terms register was not established — in particular whether records predating Regulation (EU) 2017/1129 (i.e. pre-July 2019 approvals under the old prospectus directive regime) remain searchable.

Ultimate beneficial ownership for Czech payment institutions, processors and vendors is no longer obtainable from a free public source after the 17 December 2025 closure of the ESM public part and its open data.

There is no machine-readable index or bulk feed of the Sbírka listin documents, and the only official web path is rate-limited (3000 requests/day, max 50/minute) with random CAPTCHA challenges, per the ministry's published operating conditions.

The ISVR bulk open data carries a stated non-commercial usage condition and contains personal data making the recipient a GDPR controller, which is unresolved for a commercial market-intelligence use case.
Deeds filings are PDFs, frequently scanned images, and are legally required to be in Czech; there is no structured XBRL-style financial feed for unlisted Czech entities.

Small and micro entities file abbreviated statements (zkrácený rozsah) that may omit the profit-and-loss detail, and many small vendors omit or delay filing entirely despite the sanction regime; foreign banks and EU-passporting payment providers operating in CZ through a branch (odštěpný závod) or on a freedom-of-services basis may file little or nothing in the Czech deeds collection.

Documents in the collection of deeds must be drawn up and lodged in Czech, so essentially the entire disclosure corpus for this cell is Czech-only; the English-language layer is limited to guides and to a few large banks' voluntary English annual reports.

Filing timing creates a structural lag: statements are approved within 6 months and filed within 12 months of period end, and late filing is common, so the deeds collection is a 6-18 month-old view and cannot support earnings-cycle or quarterly monitoring.

The actor universe for this cell has not yet been enumerated: the NACE-code and regulator-list sweeps that would turn the register into a concrete list of CZ banking/payments companies and their suppliers were designed but not executed.

Most Czech bank EUR covered bonds and MREL paper carry XS identifiers, and Česká spořitelna's inaugural covered bond is listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange regulated market (with at least one AT-prefixed ČS instrument observed, AT0000A2STV4). The disclosure pages of the foreign listing venues — Wiener Börse, and the Luxembourg / Euronext Dublin venues typically used for XS paper — were not enumerated in this run.

Only the six ČNB-licensed covered-block issuers plus Banka CREDITAS were mapped. Other Czech deposit-takers with MREL obligations and likely bond issuance — Air Bank / PPF banka, J&T Banka, Fio banka, Trinity Bank, Max banka — and the building societies (Českomoravská stavební spořitelna, Modrá pyramida, Raiffeisen stavební spořitelna) were not systematically searched. PPF banka already surfaced as a prospectus host in one result set.

No aggregate time series of Czech covered-bond / HZL outstanding volumes was located. ČNB ARAD is the obvious candidate database but was not reached before the search budget ran out; the CDCP Fact Book and the ECBC Fact Book Czech chapter are partial substitutes.

Both ČNB registers that matter most here — the prospectus register and the final-terms register — are served by a legacy Oracle PL/SQL web application (oam.cnb.cz/sipresextdad/SIPRESWEB...) with form-driven input and no observed API, JSON endpoint, RSS or bulk export. The covered-block issuer list is a hand-maintained PDF.

Moody's and S&P covered-bond analytics for Czech programmes (ČS's inaugural bond is Moody's Aaa; KB is Fitch AAA) sit largely behind registration or subscription. Only the Fitch rating-action headline linked from KB's own investor page was reachable in this run.

Transaction announcements from deal counsel and arrangers (A&O Shearman on both the ČS EUR 500m inaugural covered bond and a UniCredit CZ&SK EUR 500m mortgage covered bond issuance; bookrunner line-ups disclosed via broker notes) proved to be a fast, well-dated channel that often describes programme structure before the issuer publishes anything. Only incidental examples were captured.

Four of the nine ČNB-listed pension companies — Allianz, UNIQA, Conseq and Rentea penzijní společnost — were captured only via the ČNB index entry and were not individually profiled or fetched in this pass. Rentea in particular is a newer entrant whose distribution model has not been characterised.

The ČNB investiční společnosti index as fetched returned only eight entities and included 'AXA investiční společnost a.s.', a name superseded by the UNIQA rebrand, while omitting REICO investiční společnost České spořitelny, which other sources show still exists. The list is therefore either partially stale or truncated in retrieval, so the bank-group investment-company population cannot be treated as settled.

The cell definition frames credit unions as sitting 'inside the same banking groups' as the other entity types. Nothing found supports this for CZ: all six ČNB-indexed spořitelní družstva (Artesa, Citfin, České spořitelní družstvo, NEY, Peněžní dům, Podnikatelská družstevní záložna) appear to be standalone cooperatives, not bank-group subsidiaries.

No check was made of whether historical annual-report PDFs remain retrievable after site migrations. Two migrations are already visible in this cell (ČMSS to csobstavebni.cz, burinka.cz to burinka.csas.cz) and a third is in progress (modrapyramida.cz to KB infrastructure), each of which typically prunes older documents.

Parent-group reporting that describes these CZ subsidiaries — KBC/ČSOB, Erste Group/Česká spořitelna, Société Générale-lineage KB, Raiffeisen Bank International, Generali CEE — was touched only incidentally through KBC group annual reports surfaced in English search, and not systematically mapped.

Several candidate URLs were carried forward from the ČNB indexes without an independent fetch — notably ČSOB Asset Management, Generali Investments CEE, Amundi CZ, NEY, Peněžní dům, Podnikatelská družstevní záložna and České spořitelní družstvo. Their document depth, formats and update cadence are therefore unknown.

The cell's entities have changed names and legal perimeters: Českomoravská záruční a rozvojová banka (ČMZRB) -> Národní rozvojová banka (NRB); Fond pojištění vkladů -> Garanční systém finančního trhu (GSFT, from 1.1.2016 under Act 374/2015 Sb., now holding both FPV and FŘK); and ČEB is being absorbed as an NRB subsidiary. Procurement platforms still file NRB under the legacy 'CMZRB' authority code.

Contracting-authority profiles were positively located for NRB (TenderArena + NEN + own page) and ČNB (E-ZAK + vhodne-uverejneni.cz), and a procurement page was located for ČEB. No procurement profile was located for EGAP, GSFT, PGRLF or the Kancelář finančního arbitra in this pass.

This cell is dominated by annual publications. Apart from MF's monthly ownership snapshots, NRB's Pillar 3 disclosures, GSFT prospectus supplements and the press feeds, there is little sub-annual quantitative disclosure — and no first-party API from any core entity.

GSFT annual reports and budgets give fund positions in PDF form, but no structured time series of Fond pojištění vkladů / Fond pro řešení krize balances, contribution rates or covered-deposit base was identified — for example in the CNB ARAD statistical database or an EU-level dataset (EBA deposit-guarantee data, EFDI).

NRB operates as a national promotional bank alongside EIF/EIB, InvestEU and Modernisation Fund instruments, and appears in at least one European Commission transport-facility programme fiche; EGAP operates within the OECD Arrangement on Officially Supported Export Credits and Berne Union reporting. None of these supranational counterpart sources were worked in this pass.

Czech terminology was established for annual reporting, disclosure, procurement, guarantees and deposit insurance. It was NOT established for the internal operating/vendor vocabulary these institutions use in tenders — e.g. core banking, card issuing/acquiring, ATM and self-service estate, payment terminal servicing, document management — which is the vocabulary a procurement-focused sweep actually needs.

Coverage focused on national-level institutions. Regional development funds, the Czech-Moravian Guarantee scheme's regional arms, Národní rozvojový fond, and municipal/regional co-financing vehicles that partner with commercial banks were not surveyed.
